title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operating in autonomous mode in Austin, Texas struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood. A human safety operator was present in the vehicle but did not intervene to prevent the collision or stop the car afterward. The system failed to recognize a slow-moving animal as an obstacle requiring evasive action or braking.

This is a failure of the vehicle's perception and planning systems operating outside conditions they were built to handle reliably. Most autonomous vehicle testing occurs on roadways where pedestrians and larger obstacles are the focus. The presence of a human operator did not serve as a checkpoint because the operator apparently did not perceive the need to intervene, or did not have time to do so.

It is not established what sensor data the vehicle possessed, whether the duck was within the vehicle's detection range at what distance, or whether faster human reaction could have prevented the outcome.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, causing significant community backlash. The self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, did not slow down or stop after hitting the duck, which residents had grown familiar with as it nested outside a local restaurant. Local residents have since placed the duck's eggs in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and stated it found no evidence supporting a resident's claim that the car failed to stop at a stop sign. In response, the company has restricted its testing operations to exclude certain streets around the lake and is now running simulations to improve the technology and prevent similar accidents in the future. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, also operate in Austin.
